purpose: Profile the remaining serial QoS 2 throughput gap (netz 27,398-29,592 vs Mosquitto 29,880 publishes/s).

capture.host_load_note: The shared 12-CPU host also ran unrelated build/test jobs during this capture; ranking is from 2,048 samples with zero losses, but absolute cycle shares are approximate.

conclusions: No single netz protocol function dominates the serial QoS 2 cost.

Zio event-loop, executor, scheduler and clock work account for roughly a quarter of sampled cycles: __kernel_clock_gettime 11.67%, Executor.run 3.84%, AnyTask.yield 3.31%, processCleanup 2.97%, Loop.addInternal 2.57% and Loop.poll 1.77%.
The largest protocol-side costs are the delivery flush path (4.63%), handlePubRel (3.41%), route matching (3.18%) and packet receive/parse (2.98%).
Closing the remaining serial QoS 2 gap requires reducing per-message event-loop wakeups/clock reads or protocol work; no isolated hotspot is available for a small local patch.
